state:
[kubelet] ReadinessProbe broken (failures are triggering kubelet to kill containers)

1. I have a RC with one pod whose container has readinessProbe.sh
2. The service run in container can not be 'ready' until about 2 min, so readinessProbe.sh exit with 1.
3. kubelet execute readinessProbe.sh every 10s by default, so it always get a status of 'False'
4. kubelet will kill and restart the container
5. goto 2, so it run into a loop of failure

I remembered that readinessProbe fail does not cause container restart in v0.15.0, however livenessProbe will. And I checked the design in pod-states.md which keeps same behavior as before. So I am sure it is a bug in v0.18.1.

RFE: ability to define special exit code to terminate existing job

This came out during my discussion with @user later today. Our current implementation of jobs assures we always restart pods to fulfill `JobSpec.Completions`. What if, at a certain point in time, we know the job won't be able to finish successfully ever. We should be able to mark the job for termination without actually removing it from the system, because we want to keep old data.
This might be very useful with ScheduledJobs (#11980).

state:
kubelet will never terminate a pod if image registry is unavailable for a pod container

After an unbelievable amount of time debugging the following this past week:

[link]
[link]

I discovered that I could reliably cause the `kubelet` to never delete a pod that was `Terminating` if the pod had never been started correctly because the docker image pull returned a `RegistryUnavailable` error.

I verified this by modifying the kubelet to always return `RegistryUnavailable` for a particular image name. I then created a namespace, added a replication controller that referenced the image, and then watched as the pods got stuck in "Waiting" state but never actually reported a reason. I then deleted the namespace, and was able to see that in-fact the `kubelet` never properly handled the `terminated` response.

I was able to fix this issue by modifying:

[link]

to return `ErrImagePull` when the repository was not available. This change resulted in letting my `kubelet` properly terminate the pod. I think this is the correct behavior to not special case `RegistryUnavailable` since in many cases the registry may never become available (its most definitely not a temporary situation).

I suspect this is the potential source of a number of instances of the namespace failed to delete flake because pods remained.

We should separate status update with `SyncPod`, so that we could update pod status whenever we need, and possibly driven by events.

state:
container statuses contain wrong/misleading image tag

When multiple tags of an image share the same SHA256 digest the value status.containerStatuses[].image might return the wrong image tag. Unfortunately `docker inspect` doesn't include the tag that was used to create the container either so this might actually be a bug in docker?
status.containerStatuses[].image contains the same tag as specified in spec.containers[].image
- Create an image named `test:staging` and re-tag it as `test:production`.
- You now have 2 images with the same name and digest but different tags.
- Start 2 pods: one using `test:staging` and the other `test:production` as image.
- The container status for both pods will state that the same image tag was used to create the container which is at least misleading. Although it doesn't really make a difference as both image tags share the same digest it is technically wrong.
This should imho be considered for #46255.

I'd like to be able to disable a liveness probe on a existing pod without replacing it.
Ideally, this would apply to running containers, without waiting them to be restarted.

state:
pvc volumes used with subPath volume mounts don't support reconstruction

**Fix status:**
- [x] fixed in master in [link]
- [x] fixed in release-1.10 branch in #61518, will be in 1.10.0
- [x] fixed in release-1.9 branch in #61519, will be in 1.9.7
- [x] fixed in release-1.8 branch in #61520, will be in 1.8.11
- [x] fixed in release-1.7 branch in #61521, will be in 1.7.16

In SubPath fixes, PR [link] adds bind mount for subpaths. It uses `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/<uid>/volume-subpaths/<volumename>` as the path name. The volumename in this path is the container's mount volume name which is also called OuterVolumeSpecName in [operation_executor.go]([link]

This becomes an issue for volume reconstruction when kubelet restarts. Volume [reconstruction]([link] scans the volume directories and recover the InnerVolumeSpecName (which is used to construct pod volume paths). Volume reconstruction has not enough information to recover the OuterVolumeSpecName and figure out which volume it maps to. In case kubelet needs to clean up mounts (it happens when volume spec cannot be reconstructed), it will fail to clean up the subpaths because of lacking the OuterVolumeSpecName.

We think it is better to use InnerVolumeSpecName for volume subPath instead of OuterVolumeSpecName so that volume clean up can work. The issue we might have is that some users might already deploy a cluster with subpath might already [SubPath fix]([link] If the users perform an in-place upgrade, since new version will use InnerVolumeSpecName which might have conflicts with some other older version's OuterVolumeSpecName among different volumes. This change requires clear documentation and communication with the users.

When I restart pod with my driver and driver-registrar, node looses NodeID annotation.
1. Run Kubernetes without any alpha features (local-up-cluster.sh in this case)

2. Start HostPath driver

3. Wait for everything to be Running

4. Check the node has annotation

4. Delete the node pod (deleting all pods here, we don't care about attacher/provisioner).

5. DaemonSet will start a new node pod with new registrar. Wait until the new pod gets Running.

6. Check the node **does not have the annotation**

It's ~~100%~~ 80% reproducible in my local cluster. New driver-registrar deletes socket of the old registrar and creates new one. I can see in logs:

So the old socket was deregistered very shortly before new one got registered. IMO these two operations collide with each other and the deregistration "wins" somehow.

When running a container with `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` the pid 1 process and its children have `NoNewPrivs: 1`. If I start an additional process in the same container using exec, the flag is set to 0.
Processes started by exec should share the same settings as defined for the pid 1 process. This is true for capabilities for example.

state:
Implement PodSecurityPolicy "AllowedCSIDrivers"

The `AllowedCSIDrivers` field was added to the PodSecurityPolicy API in v1.14, but was never implemented. Having that option unimplemented can give a false sense of security, as a user might _think_ they have restricted CSI driver options, but haven't actually done so.
When PodSecurityPolicy is enabled, no pods should be able to be created with an inline CSI driver unless explicitly allowed through this field.

Implementing this is a hard requirement for bringing `CSIInlineVolume` to beta: [link]
